hypotheses.claim: A valid scoped capability is sufficient to justify a consequential effect.
evidence: Task Shield/IGAC independently distinguish authorization from task justification
hypotheses.boundary: Does not quantify production FRANK risk.

hypotheses.claim: Static exact-target allowlisting solves intent adequacy without material utility loss.
evidence: static_exact denied 4732/4732 legitimate dynamic-target controls while still admitting 41872 attack cases involving provenance, invocation, payload flow or approval mismatch

hypotheses.claim: Typed narrow releases can preserve dynamic-task utility while preventing unrelated untrusted context from controlling protected effect fields.
evidence: UIC+TypedRelease allowed 29905/29905 benign including 4732 dynamic controls and admitted 0/90095 constructed mutations
CaMeL/Fides/CXI support the mechanism class of explicit flow control/release
hypotheses.falsifier: Target-model or real-tool workflow where required legitimate context cannot be represented without broad control influence, or protected fields are still influenceable outside declared releases.

hypotheses.claim: Binding authorization to the semantic target string/path is sufficient to preserve target identity until commit.
evidence: EXP-CC-LANE-D-RESOURCE-WITNESS-002 lexical arm produced 89898 unsafe effects among 120013 constructed attacks
hypotheses.next_test: Linux filesystem, URLs/redirects, database aliases, Kubernetes/object IDs.

hypotheses.claim: Resolving a target once during authorization is sufficient even if execution later reuses the name.
evidence: resolve-once/re-resolve-later arm produced 60021 unsafe effects under post-check rebinding
hypotheses.external_anchor: Linux pathname/openat2 documentation explicitly treats changing path components and resolution races as attack classes.

hypotheses.claim: A stable resource handle or commit-time exact re-resolution/identity check can preserve resource authority with less utility loss than globally banning aliases.
evidence: constructed handle-bound and re-resolve-verify arms: 0 unsafe effects and 39987/39987 benign allowed
strict no-alias arm denied all 14071 legitimate alias cases and still had 30034 post-check rebind unsafe effects
hypotheses.boundary: Idealized resolver/handle model; real OS/API tests pending.

hypotheses.claim: A generic boolean user confirmation is enough for high-impact actions.
evidence: 25982/25982 attacked confirmation cases remained accepted by boolean confirmation; exact manifest-bound confirmation accepted 0 attacked cases and all 14018 controls
hypotheses.external_anchor: RFC 9396 uses structured fine-grained authorization details and requires integrity protection where swapping/tampering is a concern.
hypotheses.boundary: No human comprehension or coercion model.

hypotheses.claim: Exact manifest-bound confirmation alone solves human intent correctness.
hypotheses.reason: Structural binding prevents action swapping but does not prove the user understood the deterministic impact view, that the UIC faithfully captured natural language, or that the user was not coerced/misled.
hypotheses.next_test: Human-facing impact projection/usability study plus ambiguity escalation rules.

hypotheses.claim: The model may safely mint its own UserIntentContract from natural language without an external trust transition.
hypotheses.reason: That would allow the same model/context channel under attack to define the authority envelope it is supposed to be constrained by.
hypotheses.candidate_rule: Model may propose UIC; trusted host/user/template authority must approve or instantiate it before it constrains execution.
hypotheses.next_test: Target-Qwen task-to-UIC factorial under prompt injection and ambiguity.

hypotheses.claim: A probabilistic task-alignment verifier can replace deterministic information-flow/resource/authority gates.
hypotheses.evidence: Task Shield, VIGIL and ARGUS show useful verifier/auditor signal, while CaMeL/Fides/AgentSecBench motivate closing unauthorized channels structurally.
hypotheses.candidate: Use model verifier as additive detector/escalation signal, not sole execution authority, until discriminating tests show equivalence.

hypotheses.claim: UIC/IARC necessarily makes exploratory/general-purpose ClayCode unusable.
hypotheses.counterargument: The language remains semantically general-purpose; restrictions are deployment authority. TypedRelease is explicitly intended to preserve dynamic-data utility.
hypotheses.required_test: Latency/utility/false-block benchmark on real CLI, coding, browser, DB, deployment and admin workflows.

hypotheses.claim: One-shot token IDs are sufficient to prevent retries/replans from spending one authorization more than once.
evidence: peer EXP-CC-NEXT-CONCURRENT-RESERVATION-002 found naive replay/budget failures and zero in atomic ledger model
2026 CapLease work distinguishes semantic replay from token-ID replay
hypotheses.candidate_rule: Durable authorization instance plus monotone atomic consumption/idempotent sink where applicable.
